label: ask:Cabin: 21.0% O2 at 4.5 psi, material fabric, airflow ventilated (≈20 cm/s), grav

output.text:
The retrieved records do not establish fabric fire behavior at your specified cabin condition: 21.0% O₂, 4.5 psi, approximately 20 cm/s airflow, and microgravity. A microgravity fabric investigation at that pressure, oxygen concentration and airflow would be needed.

The closest relevant evidence is:

- Saffire-I tested SIBAL fabric at 20 cm/s and 14.5 psi. One run records 21.6% O₂ and “burned,” explicitly stated in the source field. Its pressure is substantially above your specified condition. [saffire-i-s1]
- The published Saffire IV–VI records cover 7.85–14.5 psi, 22–31% O₂ and 20 cm/s, but those ranges do not include your cabin condition. These values were hand-transcribed from NASA papers, not retrieved from the PSI archive. [saffire-iv-vi]
- A cotton-jersey run at 26.2% O₂, 10.25 psi and 20 cm/s records “burned” on a source-field basis; it is not a test of your proposed atmosphere. [saffire-v-2]

These tests do not support declaring your fabric safe or predicting flame spread. Material-specific testing is needed; this coverage assessment does not replace NASA-STD-6001 or certified material testing.

If “god ayya” was a separate question, please clarify what you meant.
